**What type of PR is this?**
> Uncomment only one ` /kind <>` line, hit enter to put that in a new line, and remove leading whitespace from that line:
/kind bug

**What this PR does / why we need it**:
When multiple securityGroups is used on AWS CLB type service, one of the securityGroup will be chosen for granting inbound access to worker nodes(which will also be removed upon service deletion). However, the chosen one is non-deterministic due to it relies on the securityGroup order by ELB API.
This PR makes the logic deterministic by always choose the first one. 

With this PR:
* if `service.beta.kubernetes.io/aws-load-balancer-security-groups` are used with multiple securityGroups, only the first one need to be unique per service.
* if `service.beta.kubernetes.io/aws-load-balancer-extra-security-groups` are used, they don't need to be unique per service.The global.ElbSecurityGroup or auto_created one will be used
* if no annotation presents. The global.ElbSecurityGroup or auto_created one will be used

Thanks to @albertofem, which solve a subset of this problem: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/90487

**Which issue(s) this PR fixes**:
<!--

-->
Fixes https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/92225
Fixes https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/84926
**Special notes for your reviewer**:
* tested via kops for three scenario, and the behaviors is as expected(first securityGroup returned by buildELBSecurityGroupList is chosen as inbound SG to worker nodes)
   *  use no annotation
   * use `service.beta.kubernetes.io/aws-load-balancer-security-groups`
   * use `service.beta.kubernetes.io/aws-load-balancer-extra-security-groups`

issue_context.body:
<!-- Please use this template while reporting a bug and provide as much info as possible. Not doing so may result in your bug not being addressed in a timely manner. Thanks!

If the matter is security related, please disclose it privately via https://kubernetes.io/security/
-->


**What happened**:
When multiple securityGroup are specified for AWS ELB type service, a random one will be chosen to grant inbound access to worker node.

**What you expected to happen**:
Always first LoadBalancer securityGroup be chosen to access worker nodes.

**How to reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)**:
use `service.beta.kubernetes.io/aws-load-balancer-security-groups` or `service.beta.kubernetes.io/aws-load-balancer-extra-security-groups` on aws elb.

**Anything else we need to know?**:

**Environment**:
- Kubernetes version (use `kubectl version`): <=1.18
- Cloud provider or hardware configuration: aws
- OS (e.g: `cat /etc/os-release`): linux
- Kernel (e.g. `uname -a`): linux
- Install tools: kops/eks
- Network plugin and version (if this is a network-related bug):
- Others:
